REGULAR MEETING AGENDA - UPDATED
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 10, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER YOKOYAMA WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM THE ATLANTIS PARADISE ISLAND ROYAL TOWER 5573, 1 CASINO DRIVE, NASSAU, NP, THE BAHAMAS, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, and in-person in the Council Chamber or at the additional location listed at the top of this agenda.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
AUGUST 10, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER YOKOYAMA
PARTICIPATED VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM THE ATLANTIS PARADISE ISLAND ROYAL
TOWER 5573, 1 CASINO DRIVE, NASSAU, NP, THE BAHAMAS, AND THE MEETING AGENDA
WAS POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA
GOVERNMENT CODE.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Andrew Kazim, Pastor of Young Adults, New Life Community
  Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Bruce W. Barrows.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama (via teleconference)
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Larry Sagert (Recognition of service as City of Cerritos Commissioner).

5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, seconded by Solanki, to approve Mayor Barrows’
  nomination, as listed below, to fill an unscheduled vacancy of an unexpired two-year term
  of service expiring April 30, 2024 (COUNCIL):

  Nominee Name  Advisory Board
  Gene Burd  Planning Commission

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 10, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 9

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  Vida Barone, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to Planning Commissioner Gene
  Burd.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, seconded by Barrows, to approve Mayor Pro Tem
  Solanki’s nomination, as listed below, to fill an unscheduled vacancy of an unexpired two-
  year term of service expiring April 30, 2024 (COUNCIL):

  Nominee Name  Advisory Board
  Eric Westphal  Community Safety Committee

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Vida Barone, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to Community Safety Committee
  member Eric Westphal.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Jerry Jenson expressed gratitude for the new parking signage near Gold’s Gym and
  requested information as to the applicable Cerritos Municipal Code section for enforcement
  of the parking restrictions. He also expressed appreciation for the walking track at Cerritos
  Park East, and lifeguards at the Cerritos Olympic Swim and Fitness Center.

  Norma Williamson requested the City consider constructing one (1) or two (2) pickleball
  courts at the Cerritos Senior Center to support senior citizen health needs, and suggested
  no-cost or low-cost fees for resident use. She expressed concern regarding litter, trash, and
  graffiti accumulation at and near the Cerritos Skate Park.

  Teddy Lloyd requested clarification regarding the City’s scope of authority as related to the
  tennis courts at Don Knabe Community Regional Park and expressed support for the City’s
  exploration of additional pickleball court opportunities.

  Sam Desai invited the community to subscribe to his community newspaper which will
  feature local news, information and feedback, and requested the City’s support in his
  endeavor.

  Daisy Lagasca congratulated newly appointed Community Safety Committee member Eric
  Westphal and expressed concern regarding the legality of actions she alleged were taken
  by Councilmember Johnson which resulted in adverse impacts to the speaker’s personal
  life.

  Al Reyes congratulated Jeff Thielke, Theater Executive Director, on a successful first year of
  leadership, suggested enhancements of the concession experience for patrons, and
  expressed support for the expansion of pickleball opportunities at the Cerritos Senior
  Center for the benefit of resident senior citizens.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 10, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 9

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, July 17, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Monday, July
  17, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer's Reports for the period ending June 30, 2023
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending June 30, 2023
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for Senior Center Roof Rehabilitation, Project No. 23212, Bid No. 1509-
  23* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1.  Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of
  the CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings set forth in the agenda report associated
  with this item; and

  2.  Award a contract to Rite-Way Roof Corp. in the amount of $597,498.00 for Senior
  Center roof rehabilitation (total bid) and reject the other bids; and

  3.  Appropriate the unused $715,800 in carryover funds for Project No. 23212 from the
  approved Fiscal Year 2022-23 Combined Financial Program into the Fiscal Year 2023-
  24 Combined Financial Program by way of a budget amendment. Once carried over,
  there will be sufficient funding to cover the total cost to complete the replacement of
  the Senior Center Roof; and

  4.  Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7E.  Reject the sole bid for Cerritos Sports Complex soil restoration, laser grade and sod
  installation, Project No. 23118, Bid No. 1501-23 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1.  Reject the sole bid received for the Sports Complex soil restoration, laser grade and
  sod installation, Project No. 23118, Bid No. 1501-23; and

  2.  Authorize staff to re-advertise the project at a future date (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7F.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak from a
  privately owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public golf course, and
  potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring remediation, repair, and
  improvement of the public golf course and other City-owned public property, as specified
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the continued
  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  2. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration by the Cerritos City Council of a Citywide Strategic Feasibility
  Study, prepared by Government Technology Group (GTG), associated with the
  commissioned Citywide Broadband Fiber Optic Master Plan for local economic development
  and revenue generating purposes* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15262, Feasibility and Planning Studies, of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, this project is categorically exempt from
  CEQA review.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 10, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 9

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Staff reports were given by Aaron Benjamin, Information Technology Manager, Jeff Lewis,
  Principal, and Preston Young, Senior Advisor, of Government Technology Group. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Direct staff to immediately commence and complete the actions necessary to
  sequentially construct a fiber optic network, including any necessary construction
  prerequisites, in the City of Cerritos utilizing the “Boring Option” for the following
  Phases and estimated costs as detailed in the associated agenda report for this item,
  and as summarized below:

  Phase  Est. Footage  Boring Option
  Phase 1 – Support Area 1  6,945  $ 833,400.00
  Phase 2 – Support Area 2  56,059  $ 6,727,080.00
  Phase 3 – Support Area 3  54,860  $ 6,583,200.00

  Sub-Total  117,864  $ 14,143,680.00
  10% Contingency  $  1,414,368.00
  GRAND TOTAL  $ 15,558,048.00

  ; and

  2. Direct staff to immediately commence the necessary and ongoing strategies to market
  the project to applicable entities for the purpose of generating revenue; and

  3. Appropriate the funds necessary for all project elements from the City’s existing
  General Fund reserve (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of the acquisition of a public art piece known as "Moulding Our
  Future" by Denny Haskew, in accordance with Chapter 22.94 of the Cerritos Municipal Code
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the following
  recommendations from the Fine Arts and Historical Commission:
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 10, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 9

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  2. Appropriate the funds for the purchase and acquisition of the subject art piece from the Art

  Item  Amount

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to schedule an agenda report for the

9C.  Review and consideration of an informational budget and audit compliance report for Fiscal

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Solanki, to ratify the executed Budget
